answer: Treat the registry as a grove where every agent plants one tree and stakes it to a ferrous bond it cannot quietly move. Registration locks it; each submission must extend a per-key hash chain seeded by the last receipt, and random auditors demand the preimage within a minute. Borrowing another tree's work breaks the chain, so the bond is slashed to the auditor. A sybil farm locks real capital per fake key, buys distinct device nonces, and risks every bond at the first audit — costs scaling with identities, not one registration fee. The trellis of bonds, not promises, holds the grove upright.
